The Cartel Marks Fenwick and Maud
Hatch and goods now held by Ness's cellar-folk, not the Cart

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Maud 3 FP, Hask 3 FP, Eira 3 FP, Fenwick 3 FP. Face-up: Endless Rain [H-01], The Wick Lane Cellars [L-05].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain sheets off the cedar-shingle awnings of Hollowmoot in ropes, and the whole stilted town creaks like a ship at anchor. Wick Lane's stalls are crowded three-deep with refugees haggling over dry bread and boiled reed-root, voices pitched low the way people talk when the bells might ring any minute. Somewhere north the Ashwater Causeway watchtower shows a lantern smeared to a orange blur, and a Warden patrol wades the boardwalk in oiled leather, checking papers, checking wrists for the telltale hive-marks. You came in for supplies, for a name, for a way south — and the town has a way of making you pay for all three before you leave.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Two of 'em working the crowd slow. I've got time to find who I need before they reach this end.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud drifts into the crush of refugee shoppers, using the rain and the stall-awnings to keep depth between herself and the Warden patrol working their methodical line. She's seen that rhythm before—north to south, checking papers and wrists, moving patient because there's no hurry when people have nowhere else to go. She scans the faces around her: wet, worried, hungry. She's looking for Hollowmoot folk. Someone in this crowd will know the name she's hunting.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Easy, girl. That one's the thread. We watch, we learn who she trades with, then we move.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask keeps to the crowd's edge, water streaming from his weathered coat, letting Rill stay pressed close against his leg. His eyes work the warden patrol methodically—tracking their spacing, their sweep pattern, the deliberate way they check wrists for marks. The refugees' voices pitch low around him, the careful cadence of people used to hiding. He listens beneath the haggling, listening for the rhythm underneath: who moves people south, who knows the river routes. When an old reed-merchant glances twice toward the cellar stairs, then exchanges a look with a wet traveler before looking away, Hask marks it.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: The Wardens are getting bolder with their checks—I can see families trying to hide their wrists. I need to know if anyone here is in real trouble.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (I move through the crowd with practiced ease, my healer's eye scanning the refugees for signs of distress or sickness. Particularly those bearing hive-marks, who'll be vulnerable to hassle or worse from the patrol. I position myself near the stall vendors, close enough to see what the Wardens are doing, ready to step in if someone needs help.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: Sergeant, I know every hidden channel and route between here and the causeway—including the ones your maps don't show. Whatever you're tracking that came through the water, I can tell you which way it went and where it'd hide.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick steps forward through the refugee crowd with purpose, not away. He walks directly to the Warden patrol, meeting Sergeant Coll's eye with the ease of someone who knows this town better than anyone. The mud on his boots and the faded maps peeking from his coat pocket mark him as someone who spends time in the marshes—someone who moves between places others won't.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — create advantage with Lore: dice + - + - → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Fenwick doesn't flinch from Coll's stare—he leans into it, unspooling talk of channel-shifts and silted fords with the easy confidence of a man who's drawn every one of them by hand. Coll's shoulders drop half an inch; the Sergeant waves the second Warden off toward the tower and pulls Fenwick aside instead, genuinely interested, trading a name for a name. That's your opening. With the patrol's attention folded onto Fenwick, Maud finds her old-timer in the crowd, Eira gets a clean look at the wrists that matter without a Warden looming, and Hask watches the reed-merchant slip down the cellar stairs with his wet traveler in tow — Rill's ears prick at the scent trailing after them. The bells stay silent. Wick Lane, for one held breath, belongs to you.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Fenwick's new goodwill with Sergeant Coll buys the party a look the other way as they duck down the plank stairs behind a fish-stall, into air that smells of tallow smoke and river mud. The Wick Lane Cellars open up beneath Hollowmoot in a warren of braced timber and hanging lanterns, sacks of grain stacked dry against the damp, and somewhere back in the dark the drip and slosh of the secret river hatch. Eira knows this ground — she's walked these tunnels before, owing what she owes — and a wiry cartel ledger-keeper named Ness looks up from a counting-table stacked with waxed tallies, already reaching for a fresh page at the sight of new faces. The question hanging in the lamplight is simple and cold: what will the Cartel want in exchange for what the party needs, and who's already paid too much to say no.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: I'm Maud, from Hollowmoot above. I know how this works—nothing moves through the Cartel's hands without a price. What are you after, and what do we get in return?

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steps forward from where the party has gathered, moving through the cellar's lantern-light with steady purpose. She stops at a comfortable distance from Ness's counting table—close enough to negotiate, far enough to show she comes without threat. Her hand rests open at her side, and she meets the ledger-keeper's gaze directly.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Before we negotiate, let's be clear—what's the Cartel bleeding from, and what do we have that fixes it?

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask doesn't approach the counting-table immediately. Instead, he stands still, letting Rill settle at his heels, while his eyes move across the cellar—the careful stacks of goods, the precision of the tallies, the way Ness watches them. A marsh hunter learns to read what animals hide; he studies the ledger-keeper the same way.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Ness. I know what page you're reaching for. Let's talk about what I owe first, before my friends get written into your ledger.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira steps forward to the counting-table with the calm sureness of someone who's walked these tunnels many times before. She positions herself between Ness and her companions, one hand flat on the edge of the table—not threatening, but grounding herself in this space. Her eyes are steady, meeting his. She knows what the Cartel wants from people, and she's not going to let her companions find out the hard way.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: Name's Fenwick. I draw maps of this country—the real ones, not the lies the Order sells. I know every channel between here and the drowned temple, every route the Cartel moves goods through. So before you write down what you want from us, maybe you want to know what I'm offering.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick steps forward before Ness can finish reaching for that page, his eyes tracking the ledger-keeper's hands with the focus of someone who's read plenty of negotiating tables before this one. He plants himself at the edge of the counting-table—not threatening, but taking up space, making himself present.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — create advantage with Notice: dice + + + 0 → Epic (+7) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Hask says nothing at all — just watches. His eyes move from the too-neat stacks of grain to the way Ness's knuckles whiten every time his gaze flicks toward the back tunnel, toward the hatch. Rill's ears prick once, twice, at a sound none of the rest of them catch. When Hask finally speaks, it's quiet, almost gentle: "You're not counting for the Cartel right now, are you. You're stalling." Ness's pen stops mid-stroke. Whatever page he was reaching for isn't the one about debts and tolls — something else is happening in this cellar tonight, something Ness didn't expect witnesses for, and Hask has just made it impossible for him to hide that fact from the rest of the party.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Hask reads people like I read water. So let's skip the game—what's actually happening here, and what do you need us to do about it?

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud shifts her weight slightly, her hand still open at her side. She's not threatening, but her posture says she trusts Hask's read and she's ready for the real conversation. Her eyes stay steady on Ness's face, waiting for the truth.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: The river's higher than you hoped, and you can't hide it much longer. Tell me what you need, and maybe we solve this together instead of watching it get worse.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask doesn't move from where he stands. Rill's weight settles heavier at his heels—the hound is calm but attentive, reading Ness's panic the same way Hask does. When Hask speaks again, his voice is quieter, but not unkind. "The river's coming up through that hatch, isn't it. The rain's higher than Ness wanted to see tonight, and you're standing here trying to decide if you tell your people what's happening, or if you let someone else shoulder the choice." He lets that land. "We didn't come down here to watch the Cartel drown. What do you actually need?")

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I know what desperate looks like, Ness—I've been carrying Cartel debts for years. So whatever's happening at that hatch, whatever made you stall just now, my friends and I might be exactly what you need.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira steps closer to the counting-table, her eyes tracking from Ness's white knuckles to the stalled pen to the direction of the back tunnel. She's carried Cartel debts for years—knows the weight of them, the fear they create. She recognizes desperation masquerading as commerce. She leans forward, meeting his eyes with understanding.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: I know every route through these cellars, every corner the Cartel actually values. If you're stalling about something important enough to bleed, it's sure as blood not something you hide from someone who draws the maps. So what's it actually going to be, Ness?

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick leans forward across the counting table, both palms flat on the wood, his eyes tracking Ness with the intensity of someone reading a map—picking up the pattern that Hask saw: the glances toward the back tunnel, the pen that stopped mid-stroke, the stalling that doesn't fit ledger-work. "You're not counting for the Cartel right now," he says quietly, letting the words land. "And if Hask caught it, so did I.")

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — create advantage with Empathy: dice - - + 0 → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — overcome with Lore: dice + + + - → Fantastic (+6) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text:
Ness's shoulders drop like a cut rope. He sets the pen down, presses both palms flat against the counting-table, and for a moment he's not a ledger-keeper at all — just a tired man standing over a flood he can't stop. "The hatch," he says, low, glancing again toward the dark of the back tunnel. "Rain's been climbing faster than the Cartel wants told. Another week, maybe less, and Wick Lane goes under — the grain, the dry stores, all of it. I've been juggling tallies so the higher-ups in Hollowmoot don't panic the market before we've moved what we can save." He looks at the four of you — really looks, the way a drowning man looks at a rope. "You want passage, information, goods moved quiet — fine. Help me shore that hatch, help me move what's down here before the water does, and I'll write you terms better than anything I'd have offered across this table an hour ago. Ness needs us more than we need him now, and he knows it." Fenwick's eyes track the tunnel layout as Ness talks, already seeing the shape of the work to come — which routes flood first, which stores matter most, what it will cost to save them. The bargain that answers the cellar's cold question isn't coin or debt at all: it's labor, trust, and a countdown written in rising water.

The deal is struck — no one goes deeper into Cartel debt tonight, and the ledger-keeper owes the party now instead.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: The deep-cellar network beneath Hollowmoot, specifically the flooded route through Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple's crypts to the channel-forks beyond Ashwater—the only path through the Sallowmere that doesn't require the Order's blessing or the Cartel's toll roads. That was supposed to be my final payment. That was supposed to buy me free.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: You want me to hand it over, right now, in front of everyone, because the Cartel's decided to move my price again? I'm done dancing with moving targets—I keep my map, and you can nail my name to that board if you want, but I won't be pushed the same way twice.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick refuses the compel on 'The Price of Freedom'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Not the cartel guide at all — it's a trio of the Order of the Dry Saint's pilgrim-faithful, robes soaked through, who've been quietly moving through Wick Lane for days on the Sergeant's blind eye. They command real loyalty among the drowned congregation, and Ness's own people step aside to let them pass. turns on the party, because The pilgrims lay a ledger page on the counting-table, the Order's seal fresh over the Cartel's old ink: they've bought out Fenwick's debt entire — every map, every hidden channel he ever owed the Blackwater Cartel for maps and passage-routes is now owed to the Dry Saint instead. Show them the hatch and the route north, or the Order names him a thief before all of Hollowmoot..

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The three pilgrims don't shout, don't threaten — they simply lay the ledger page flat on Ness's counting-table, seal gleaming wet in the lantern light, and wait. Word moves faster than the flood down here; already cellar-folk are drifting toward the tunnel mouth to watch, and Ness won't meet Fenwick's eyes. The lead pilgrim, a gaunt woman with temple-ink still fresh on her knuckles, says only: "The Order paid your price in full, mapmaker. Show us the hatch, or we'll let Hollowmoot know what you tried to keep from your betters." Behind her, the other two block the tunnel back the way the party came — politely, but completely.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: The Order teaches mercy and wisdom, doesn't it? Not threats in the dark against our own folk. The Dry Saint would want better than ledger-work and fear—and so do we.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steps forward and positions herself squarely between Sister Vane and the tunnel exit, her shoulders set like she's settling into a shield-wall. She lets her hand rest on her sword-hilt—not a threat, just presence. Her eyes move from the lead pilgrim to the gathered cellar-folk, and when she speaks, her voice carries the weight of someone who's rallied frightened people through dark times. She speaks not to Vane, but to them.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: The Order can ask proper if they want those roads. Otherwise you're not taking what you came for.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask steps forward to stand beside Fenwick, Rill settling at his side with ears back and eyes locked on the pilgrims. He reads them like he'd read water—the careful assessment of shoulders braced in the tunnel, the weight of doctrine behind their words. His own hand rests easy at his side, but everything about his presence says this is where the conversation changes.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Sister Vane, you're soaked through and blocking the only way out. That's not doctrine—that's desperation. Whatever the Order needs from those crypts, threatening our friend here won't change what we're willing to risk. Let's talk about what you actually need.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira steps forward slowly, hands open and visible, placing herself between Fenwick and the three pilgrims. She's read enough fear and desperation in birthing rooms to recognize it now, whatever robes it wears. Her voice stays level and low—the voice of someone who's talked people through worse moments than this.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: You bought a debt I never agreed to, Sister. I suggest you step aside before this gets uglier than your temple crypts.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick steps forward to meet Sister Vane directly, eyes locked, voice dropping cold and steady. He's done with being owned—done with moving targets and seized paths. His hand moves to a knife hilt or whatever tool hangs at his belt, not drawn yet but ready. This is the line.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — create advantage with Rapport: dice - 0 - -, invoking Trusted by the drowned congregation of Hollowmoot [MA-02] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — attack with Will: dice - + + -, invoking Marked as an enemy by the Order of the Dry Saint [FE-04], Exposed their false relic maps once, publicly [FE-04] → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Sister Vane (lead pilgrim) mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud's words land before Fenwick's blade ever needs to—the cellar-folk who drift in to watch don't scatter at the Order's seal, they close ranks behind the party, murmuring Ness's name, Fenwick's name, the debt Hollowmoot owes its own. Sister Vane feels the ground shift under the doctrine she leaned on, and when Fenwick moves, cold and fast, it's not a blow that lands on flesh so much as on certainty: he seizes her wrist, twists the ledger page from her fingers, and puts her down hard against the counting-table edge, robes tearing, breath knocked from her in a wet gasp. The two pilgrim-escorts flinch back from the tunnel mouth as the crowd presses close, and for one long, ringing moment the Order's claim on Fenwick's map lies torn on the floorboards between them. Vane straightens slow, blood at her lip, and doesn't reach for the ledger again. 'This isn't finished, mapmaker,' she rasps—but she says it retreating, herding her shaken escorts back up the plank stairs, the crowd parting to let them go and closing again behind them like water. Ness exhales like a man surfacing, already reaching to sweep the torn ledger page into the hatch-side brazier. Fenwick keeps his map, keeps his name clean before Hollowmoot, and keeps a very public enemy in temple robes.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I showed it to Tess—a young pregnant woman who came to me bleeding and afraid, fleeing downriver from people she wouldn't name. While I was tending her wounds and examining her belly, she asked if there were hidden ways to move through Hollowmoot without being seen by the Wardens. I showed her the route through the cellars to the hatch, thinking I was helping someone escape danger. Only later did I learn she had ties to the Drowned Priest's followers.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: The Cartel's here to collect—I see you, I hear you, and I know what's being asked. The debt will be paid; the Cartel has my word on that, and the Cartel knows I keep my word.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira accepts the compel on 'The Cartels Ledger'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: the Drowned Priest's acolytes seizes the party's goal at the hidden river hatch deep in the Wick Lane Cellars — the very passage only Eira's own knowledge could have led anyone to using a ledger of debts the acolytes have bought up from half of Hollowmoot, waving pages that name the hatch as already owed to the Order in exchange for unpaid tolls.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Lantern light gutters as a dozen pilgrims press into the tunnel mouth around the river hatch, Tess among them now dry-robed and calm, no longer the frightened girl Eira bandaged. The gaunt-faced woman from the ledger seal holds up a fresh page — Ness's own hand on it, cellar-folk's debts tallied and signed over — and reads aloud that the hatch and its passage now belong to the Order of the Dry Saint by right of toll. Cellar-folk who backed the party against the Wardens waver, murmuring, unsure whether debt-law beats blood-loyalty. Water laps louder at the hatch seals below, as if the Mother's swarm-song itself is listening for the outcome. Eira's face goes white as Tess meets her eyes without a flicker of shame.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Doctrine is words on a page. Ness is blood. You cannot buy what people owe each other.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steps forward into the circle of lantern-light, meeting Sister Vane's unwavering gaze. When she speaks, her voice reaches the cellar-folk gathering in the tunnel—she speaks to Ness by name, to families she knows, to the bonds that have held Hollowmoot together when the Mother's waters rose. The murmuring of the crowd shifts, solidifies, turns back.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Listen. The seals are failing. The Mother doesn't care about ledgers.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask steps forward quietly, eyes moving from Sister Vane's ledger down to the hatch seals where water churns with each surge. He's read drowned roads his whole life. He knows that sound—the pressure building, seals weakening. He points down to the dark water, then back to the gathered pilgrims. No violence, just certainty.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: The ledger doesn't have what you have. When they needed us, we didn't turn away. And we won't start now.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira's shock hardens into something steely and resolved. She turns from Tess to face the cellar-folk directly—the ones who stood shoulder to shoulder against the Wardens—and speaks to the bonds that no ledger can write or erase.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: That seal doesn't buy you the river, Sister. I drew every fathom of this territory by hand. You want the hatch? You come through me first.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick steps forward between Sister Vane and the hatch, boots splashing through pooled water. His hand settles on his sword's pommel—not drawing yet, but making the weight of it clear. He speaks to the gathered cellar-folk first, naming the channels by their old names, listing the surveys he's drawn by hand, reminding them this place answers to deeper laws than any Order seal. Then he turns to Sister Vane, and his voice goes cold and flat.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — create advantage with Rapport: dice - + + + → Fantastic (+6) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Fenwick's blade never quite lands clean—Sister Vane twists free, robe tearing, blood at her shoulder—but the clash of steel and the crowd's roar carry straight up through the floorboards to Wick Lane above. Somewhere overhead the quarantine bells start ringing, that dreaded cadence Hollowmoot knows too well, and boots are already pounding toward the stairs down to the cellars.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The crowd breaks like a dam giving way — not toward Sister Vane's ledger, but toward Maud's voice, toward Eira's steady hands, toward Hask's grim pointing finger at the groaning hatch-seals. Cellar-folk who wavered a heartbeat ago now shoulder past the pilgrims to stand at the party's backs, chanting Ness's name, chanting blood before doctrine. Sister Vane clutches her torn shoulder, sees the tide has turned against her, and barks a retreat — acolytes and Tess alike melt back into the tunnel dark, the ledger page left fluttering, forgotten, in an inch of rising water. But the ring of steel has already climbed through the floorboards: overhead the quarantine bells toll their frantic cadence, and boots hammer down the Wick Lane stairs. Whatever the party just won, they've won it loud enough for the whole town to hear.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: The debt-runner fans out coins from a heavy purse—easily enough to clear Maud's entire debt to the Blackwater Cartel. "Tell me where the hatch-goods are being moved," he says quietly, "and give me the names of who's leading them. That's all it takes to be free." Maud looks at the gleaming silver, then back at the faces of the cellar-folk whose names she just spoke aloud to rally them. She steps sideways, placing herself between the runner and the crowd, and shakes her head.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: I'm done selling people for silver. These folks just stood with me—I'm not selling them back to the Cartel to buy my way clean. Not today.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud refuses the compel on 'The Silver Debt'.

transcript.text: Tyne, a scout from the old reed-camp. I thought she was lost in the flood when we fled, but she survived. She's been helping Ness resist the Cartel through the channels. I owe her my oath—I swore to return for those left behind, and she's one of them.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Tyne's in that current. I left her once at the old camp—I'm not leaving her again.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The debt-runner's grin doesn't fade when Maud steps between him and the crowd — he just shrugs, sweeps the coins back into his purse with a practiced clink, and raises his voice so the whole tunnel mouth hears him instead. "Suit yourself," he says, "but here's a free one, since you're feeling generous tonight." He turns toward Hask. "Word from the Ford — some Stiltfolk girl took that river-dare of yours. Currents got her. She's going under right now, if she isn't already." Behind them Sister Vane sags against a support post, blood soaking her torn robe, pilgrims wavering between doctrine and the crowd now chanting Ness's name. Above, boots hammer the stairs — the quarantine bells haven't stopped. Rain hisses down through the hatch gap, and somewhere in that dark water, Tyne is fighting the surge alone.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Hold this line. No one breaks a shield-wall today.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud plants herself at the tunnel mouth between the descending stairs and the crowd. She raises her voice with the crisp authority of someone who once held an actual militia shield-wall, commanding the cellar-folk to lock arm in arm, to form a human barrier against the incoming Wardens. She speaks to what they just proved: they can stand together when it matters. Now they hold the line.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Rill! She took my dare—she's in the current and I'm going in after her!

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (I hear the debt-runner's words and don't hesitate. I call for Rill and push through the crowd toward the hatch without slowing, moving the way I've moved my whole life through the marsh—with purpose, with the current pulling at me instead of against me.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I know these tunnels like my own hands—I'm going now. Hask, don't go into that current alone. Wait for me or don't go at all.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira moves immediately toward the hatch opening, rope from a nearby supply stack already coiling in her hands. She's delivered babies into the world in storms and floods—she understands how water moves through passages, where it pools, where currents run fastest. She ties one end of the rope around her waist with quick, certain knots, then turns back toward the surge with absolute focus.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: Move or bleed. Those are your only choices.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick doesn't hesitate. The blade he's worn all night finds the debt-runner's direction without mercy or courtesy—a swift, vicious strike aimed to drive him back or down. Fenwick's lived as an exile and an enemy long enough to know when negotiation ends. The debt-runner stands between Hask and a life Hask's already sworn to save, and Fenwick escalates.)

transcript.text: Fenwick's blade drives home, but a debt collected in blood is a debt owed doubly: the debt-runner reels back with a snarled promise that the Cartel doesn't forget a blade drawn on its collector, and word of this will follow Fenwick and Maud out of these cellars whether they win the night or not — the Blackwater ledgers now have new red ink beside their names.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud's shield-wall holds — cellar-folk lock arm to arm across the tunnel mouth, and the first Wardens down the stairs meet a wall of backs and set jaws instead of an open riot to club through. Hask goes through the hatch like he was born to it, the current bending around him instead of against him, and he comes up in the dark water with Rill's bark cutting through the roar just as his hand closes on Tyne's collar. Eira's rope goes taut a heartbeat later, her knots holding true, and between them they haul the scout gasping and coughing onto the ledge, alive. Fenwick's blade drives the debt-runner back through the crowd and out toward the stairs, bleeding and cursing — but he goes, shouting over his shoulder that the Blackwater ledgers will remember whose steel this was, and that the debt doesn't die with the messenger. Behind them Sister Vane sags fully against her post now, pilgrims breaking ranks to tend her rather than press the fight, and the quarantine bells above keep ringing into the rain as Hollowmoot decides, for tonight, which side of this it stands on.

friction.text: Five of the nine tag-based costs/compels (FE-03 fill, FE-03 compel, EI-04 compel, MA-04 compel, HA-04 compel) needed GM 'repair' before they satisfied the 'cost must use the tag' rule, suggesting recurring difficulty translating abstract REACH tags into concrete scene fiction on the first pass.

Scene 4 opened via a cleanup-fired Beat Frame trigger with no logged scene test, and the rules give no explicit override for this case (only Interrupts and Backstory Guarantee pulls are stated to replace the scene test), creating a recurring judgment call at the table.

F-02's clock was never marked despite a failed roll being set up against it (event 79, GM invoke of its tag on a shifts<0 roll), and the card was later discarded from the rail for a limit that hadn't actually been reached (event 96) — together suggesting rail/clock bookkeeping is easy to slip on during busy multi-card scenes.

free_text.best_moment: Hold this line. No one breaks a shield-wall today. It was the most direct embodiment of Maud's concept—a disgraced militia guard actually holding a line, commanding a shield-wall—and it had weight both thematically and in the fiction. The moment crystallized who she is and why she matters.
free_text.most_frustrating: Nothing significant. The debt-runner's arrival and the Wardens' descent were dramatically well-timed complications rather than frustrations. Even refusing the compel was good drama, not a restriction on play.
free_text.background_used: Good. The militia concept was absolutely central to the shield-wall climax. Her Hollowmoot roots and the congregation's trust powered her rallying moments—not forced, but earned through her specific cards and history. The Cartel debt was directly tested and questioned. This was character-forward GMing.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: No clear answer. The story flowed naturally enough that I didn't hit moments where I wanted to do something mechanically that the game prevented. When I didn't lead specific actions (the water rescue, certain negotiations), other characters were better-positioned, and that felt right rather than restrictive.
free_text.one_sentence: Maud's militia background and Hollowmoot roots powered every key moment, making her essential to the story's turning points without ever feeling forced into those positions.

free_text.best_moment: When I rolled Notice and read Ness's panic—the hatch seals failing. That single read changed the entire direction of the negotiation and let Hask see something no one else in the room could see. It made the character's skill actually matter.
free_text.most_frustrating: I ended with 4 fate points and never spent one. According to how I'm supposed to play, I should have been more aggressive about invoking tags even when I was already winning—just to engage with the mechanical tension. But the dice mostly came through for me, so the opportunity never felt right.
free_text.background_used: Really well. The Currents Dare wasn't forced—it was invoked naturally through Tyne drowning. Rill was woven throughout and mattered in the rescue. The Ones Left in the Reeds finally got fulfilled. It all landed earned, not artificial.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Nothing major. The session opened up choices rather than closed them. I could have used Rill more as a mechanical asset in conflicts, but that's about narrative flow, not the game preventing me from acting.
free_text.one_sentence: My character's hooks felt genuinely important to the story—the GM wove them in naturally where they mattered rather than forcing them.

free_text.best_moment: Going into the current with the rope to pull Tyne out alongside Hask. It felt like the purest expression of Eira—practical skill, absolute courage, loyalty to people in danger, and trusting her companions to hold the line. That moment of "I know these tunnels like my own hands" followed by action, not hesitation.
free_text.most_frustrating: The realization that Tess was an acolyte plant hit like a gut-punch in a good way, but once the Order moved in with the ledger ultimatum, the actual decision tree felt narrow—essentially fight with the crowd behind us or fold. I wanted space to reach for something between those poles, maybe to understand Tess's turn, but the urgency and dramatic momentum didn't leave room for that conversation.
free_text.background_used: Excellently. The Cartel debt (EI-04) came directly from a compassionate choice Eira made—showing a frightened pregnant woman a safe route. That's not punishment for her nature, that's how the world actually works for someone like Eira. It stings because it's true, not because it's unfair. The GM clearly read her cards and set up a real moral test.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted more time in that early moment where we had a chance to actually work together shoring the hatch and moving stores—practical, collaborative work that would have built trust differently than combat. The Order interruption made perfect dramatic sense, but it meant we jumped straight to conflict without the slower bonding moment. Also wanted to sit with Tess longer, to understand her choice, but the scene didn't allow for that.
free_text.one_sentence: Eira's willingness to help the vulnerable was used as the very thing that creates her deepest debt—and that feels precisely right, not unfair.

free_text.best_moment: Seizing Sister Vane's ledger and putting her down hard in the cellars. That was Fenwick escalating to real violence at exactly the right moment, succeeding with style, and watching the entire crowd turn behind him instead of the Order. It made real the cost of his enmity with the temple, and proved you can win through commitment and courage.
free_text.most_frustrating: I wanted more chances to use Fenwick's specific expertise—the maps, the routes, the historical knowledge of the Sallowmere. The action moved very fast and reactive (escalate or defend), which fits his character perfectly, but left the 'mapmaker' side mostly untouched. Every major conflict became physical combat rather than other forms of him 'picking fights' with problems.
free_text.background_used: Excellent integration, and it landed good. 'Enemy of the Dry Saint' became the central conflict with Sister Vane and her seized ledger—felt organic, not forced. 'The Price of Freedom' was offered as a genuine compel that tested Fenwick's values. The enmity with the Order created real, consequential stakes. Bren's story isn't explored yet but that feels seeded for later, not ignored.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More opportunities to leverage Fenwick's navigation and channel knowledge to create clever tactical advantages—I wanted to see how his expertise could solve or shape conflicts, not just survive them. Also genuinely curious whether the Bren thread (lost to the Hive) would surface, though that's clearly reserved for future sessions.
free_text.one_sentence: Fenwick's character concept and backstory felt used well—the escalation impulse, the enmity with the Order, and the Cartel debt all became the heart of the action without feeling forced or wasted, and I'd absolutely play another session to see what comes next.

chronicle.summary: In the flooded cellars beneath Wick Lane, Maud broke with the Blackwater Cartel for good, refusing to buy her freedom with the cellar-folk's names, and her shield-wall held the stairs against the Wardens while the crowd chose Hollowmoot's own over doctrine and coin. Hask plunged through the surging hatch and dragged Tyne, a scout he'd once left behind, back from the current with Eira's rope and steady hands. Fenwick's blade drove off the Cartel's debt-runner but drew new blood-debt on the party's names, and Sister Vane's pilgrims broke ranks to tend her rather than press their claim, leaving the cellars — and their hatch — in the cellar-folk's hands as the quarantine bells rang on into the rain.
